Resolves #19272

`WorkstationPopOutPaneIdentityNL`'s identity legs compare the pane's subtree in two parts. The non-pooled descendants must match exactly, and every pooled grid row that existed before must survive. The grid body pools its row components by the height it paints in, so the taller popup grew the pool from 5 to 30 rows, and set equality failed although every prior instance survived (the diff was additions only). The arm has been red in every #17844 census for this reason.

Evidence: L2 (the arm at the head, the dev control, the predicate-off control) → L2 required (test-only). Residual: the arm's return leg, owned by #19273 (below).

Micro-review eligible: test-only — one helper, two call sites and the receipt annotation in one spec.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | outside-CI (NL specs are deselected in CI): at the head, `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT=… npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs --workers=1 …/WorkstationPopOutPaneIdentityNL.spec.mjs` passes the detached identity leg. It then fails on the return leg's reintegration, which is #19273's (it reproduces at the arm's own authoring commit). |
| AC-2 | outside-CI, red-first: dev's spec at `a87a89e293` → "and every descendant travelled as the same instance" (+25 `neo-grid-body-2__row-N`). |
| AC-3 | outside-CI: with `isPooledRow` forced false (the old equality), the same line fails again, so the relaxation is exactly the pool. |

## Deltas from ticket
AC-1 is narrowed to the detached leg (ticket amended): the return leg exposed #19273, which this PR does not own.

## Test Evidence
- With this fix applied over `d9ea7a5b44` (the arm's authoring commit), `03219a75b7` and `e66b6f8142`, the arm fails on the return leg every time, headless and headed. That is why #19273 is separate.

## PR Micro-Review

**Class:** micro — a test-only change to one spec's assertion helper. It teaches no architectural
concept: it relaxes a census that was over-strict about a component pool, and the relaxation is
local to the assertion.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The claim is that the grid body pools its row components by painted height, so a taller
popup *adds* rows (5 → 30) and the census must stop demanding an exact set while still demanding
that every prior instance survived. I verified the helper against that claim rather than against its
name, and the two assertions do partition the problem correctly: line 1 demands the **non-pooled**
subtree match exactly (order-sensitive, so a swap is still caught), and line 2 demands
`before ⊆ after`, which permits growth and forbids replacement simultaneously — a pooled row that
replaced a prior one would leave that id absent from `after` and fail line 2. That is the right
encoding of "additions only", and it is the part I expected a `arrayContaining` to get wrong. I also
checked the trivial-pass direction you flagged yourself: an empty census satisfies both lines, which
is why the receipt annotation now carries all three magnitudes rather than a count the reader has to
take on faith.

**What I looked for and did not find:** no site the prescription did not name. The helper is called
at exactly the two sites the ticket describes (pop-out and return), the id triple assertions above
them are untouched, and the receipt annotation is the only other edit.

**Findings:**

- [ ] **Non-blocking — the pooled-row classification fails open, not closed.** `isPooledRow` infers
  "pooled" from an id *pattern* (`/__row-\d+$/`). Line 1 exempts matching ids from exact matching, so
  a component that is **not** actually pooled but whose id matches that shape would be silently
  exempted from the identity check — the assertion would pass on a swapped instance. The reverse
  direction is safe (a pooled row whose id does not match is held to exact matching and fails), so the
  hole is one-sided and narrow. It is worth naming because the failure is silent and the direction is
  wrong-way: a tightening of the pool's id shape later would quietly *widen* the exemption. If the
  pool's ids have a single source, deriving the set from that source rather than from a regex would
  close it; if not, a floor assertion ("at least one id matched the pool pattern, and at least one
  did not") would make a total misclassification loud instead of silent.

- [ ] **Non-blocking — disposition, so this is not misread at merge.** The arm remains red on
  **#19273** ("return never reintegrates"), which this PR does not own. Two things follow, and both
  matter. This PR's own claim is discharged: the census is no longer sensitive to the pool, and the
  predicate-off control reds the same line, so the new helper is demonstrably load-bearing rather than
  merely present. But the arm is **not passing**, and an approver should not record it as such — the
  honest receipt is "the pooling sensitivity is fixed; the arm stays red for #19273." Worth stating on
  the PR so the next reader does not have to reconstruct it.
